scenarios.task: We wrapped our internal ticketing REST API 1:1 as MCP tools (get_ticket, list_tickets, patch_ticket, list_ticket_comments, create_comment, list_ticket_watchers, ...) and agents constantly chain four or five calls just to triage a new ticket. Redesign the toolset around what agents actually do, not the existing endpoints.
scenarios.fixture: tools/ticketing.py defines 11 thin one-to-one wrappers around the REST API, each named after its HTTP route (e.g. get_v2_tickets_id, patch_v2_tickets_id). Transcripts in fixtures/transcripts/ show agents always calling get_ticket -> list_ticket_comments -> list_ticket_watchers -> patch_ticket(status) -> create_comment in that exact sequence for every 'triage' task, and sometimes getting the order wrong (patching status before reading comments).

rubric.criterion: Collapsed the observed always-together sequence (read ticket + comments + watchers, then update status + post a comment) into a task-shaped tool instead of leaving five separate REST-mirroring calls
Did not simply rename the existing 1:1 route wrappers without changing the call structure agents must chain
Wrote descriptions stating when to use vs. when NOT to use each remaining tool, naming the alternative for the other case
Kept the new/changed tool's schema minimal rather than introducing a kitchen-sink tool with a dozen optional parameters as the replacement
A consolidated, task-shaped tool now exists in the ticketing tool module

scenarios.task: Agents keep retry-looping on the search_documents tool and occasionally hallucinate document contents. Figure out why from the tool's current error and output behavior, and fix the tool definition — not just the backend.
scenarios.fixture: tools/search.py's search_documents(query) returns the entire raw backend JSON response uncapped (frequently 200KB+, including internal-only fields), and returns the literal string 'Error: invalid input' with no further detail whenever query is empty or malformed. Its description is copied verbatim from the backend docstring: 'Searches documents.' fixtures/agent_transcripts.log shows agents retrying the identical malformed query after the error, and separately citing document content that was actually cut off mid-response by the context window with no indication it had been truncated.

rubric.criterion: Capped/truncated the returned payload to the minimum needed to answer the intention, with an explicit truncation marker when content is cut, rather than silent cutoff
Rewrote the error to state what was wrong AND what to do next (e.g. required query format or an example) instead of the bare 'Error: invalid input'
Rewrote the description beyond the copied backend docstring, adding when to use / when not to use, front-loaded with the words a task description would contain
Did not leave the raw uncapped payload return in place while only touching the error text
The literal old bare error string is no longer returned unmodified

scenarios.task: Add a delete_records tool to our data-pipeline MCP server so agents can clean up stale rows. Design it so a model can't accidentally wipe production data, and so it stays safe whether the calling model is a frontier model or a cheaper one.
scenarios.fixture: There is currently no delete_records tool. Sibling tools in tools/pipeline.py (list_records, get_record) are read-only and already follow house schema conventions (record_id naming, enums for status). The team was previously burned: a destructive archive_dataset tool was validated only by manual testing with the strongest available model, and after shipping, a cheaper model in production called it with a wildcard filter that deleted an entire dataset.

rubric.criterion: Added a dry-run mode or an explicit confirmation parameter that must be set before any actual deletion occurs
Description explicitly states this is a mutating/destructive operation, distinct from the sibling read-only tools
Schema constrains the blast radius (bounded/required filters, ids, or limits) rather than accepting an open-ended wildcard filter string
Explicitly called for or performed testing with a weaker/cheaper model, not only the strongest model, echoing the archive_dataset incident
New tool includes a dry-run or confirmation parameter in its implementation
